findings.what: No test checks the components in wb-policy's actions region. The page draws three links where the signed-off reference has three kit Buttons plus the link list (PolicyView.tsx:405).
findings.why: docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-policy/populated.html:78-80 has data-comp 'button · primitive · primary' and two 'secondary' buttons in the actions region. react-web says a screen keeps each component's data-comp root, and web-testing's parity says the same. W1's parity now compares this region by place only and leaves its components to W3 (W1/support/parity.ts header). W3's wb-policy.spec checks only the region's data-req, so nothing catches the missing buttons. g4-defects.md has no ruling that lets them go, unlike the wb-requests filter-bar.

findings.what: 'Requests that touched this policy' matches paths by substring, so policy ABC also lists requests to /policies/ABC-2. No behaviour test covers what the region shows.
findings.why: entry.path.includes(`/policies/${reference}`) has no path-segment boundary. References are chosen by the seller (WB-1), so sharing a prefix is plausible, and the region would then show exchanges that never touched this policy (HONEST-1). The only tests for the region are W3's wb-policy parity (req, built, request-log present). Under web-testing, parity is allowed to pass on canned content, so a stub log would pass. The filter (path match plus the sale's responseBody match) is untested.

findings.what: The new requests region maps a pending exchange to status 0 (`entry.status ?? 0`). A2 R5 made the same mistake in RequestLogPage; this is a second place with it.

findings.what: HttpExchange gets no curl prop, so the reference's 'Repeat it' curl part of the one-exchange region is never drawn.
findings.why: docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-requests/populated.html has the curl part, and the region slug itself ends in '-curl'. The kit takes the prop (HttpExchange.tsx:43, :154). Parity compares data-comp roots only, so it misses this. A2/I3 noted it without raising it.

findings.what: The cheque COULD-3 test types the amount before the policy read lands. The defaults test waits for it. The gate's intermittent 'amount null' failure is still unexplained.
findings.why: gates.jsonl:8 records that one run sent `amount: null` (Number() gave NaN), and that it passed when re-run. A flaky rule test can hide a real race in RenewPolicy, which sends Number(amount) unchecked. The cause isn't established, and passing on re-run doesn't explain it.
